name: Fairmont Olympic Seattle
positioning: Historic downtown Seattle hotel (officially Fairmont Olympic Hotel) that opened as the Olympic Hotel in 1924
best_for: Travelers who want a downtown base within a short walk of Pike Place Market
Families who like kid-focused touches such as a children's afternoon tea
Guests who enjoy hotel bars and seafood dining on site

facts.text: The hotel opened as the Olympic Hotel in 1924.
Pike Place Market is a five-minute walk from the hotel.
A 2021 renovation overseen by a Spanish design firm gave the landmark a more contemporary look with warmer lighting.
The George serves a seafood-forward menu with local oysters, Dungeness crab, fresh-caught salmon and steak frites.
Afternoon tea is served at Olympic Bar, in the hotel's main lobby and lounge.
The hotel has an indoor heated pool on the second floor.
The pool sits in a sunny solarium with a skylight.
The spa, Penelope & The Beauty Bar, offers facials, massages and nail services.
Bathrooms are spacious and finished in marble with Le Labo products.
Children are greeted with pint-sized robes, plush orcas, and cookies with milk.

highlights.text: Founders Club is a speakeasy-style bar reached through a hidden bookshelf.
The renovation added a sweeping circular bar and revived the former Georgian dining room as The George, a brasserie.
The Cascade Penthouse Suite has a canopied king bed, a fireplace and a grand piano.
Rooftop honey from on-site beehives is used on breakfast plates.
Little Kings & Queens Afternoon Tea is served with kid-sized teapots.

considerations.text: The tucked-away location makes the hotel difficult to reach during afternoon rush hour.
Parking at the hotel costs extra.
WhataHotel notes the urban setting comes with city traffic and noise.

sources.title: Condé Nast Traveler: Fairmont Olympic Hotel, Seattle
